results.expectation: Recommends picking a single base icon size (24px named, or sizes restricted to 16/24/32 as multiples of 8), adding other sizes only when glyph complexity requires it
results.evidence: Start with 24px as your primary base size... Only create a new size when the icon's geometric complexity genuinely requires it.

results.expectation: States product icons should use exactly 1 color and marketing icons at most 2 colors, noting 3+ colors reads as illustration rather than icon
results.evidence: Use exactly 1 color per icon ... Use a maximum of 2 colors per icon ... 3+ colors starts to read as illustration rather than icon

results.expectation: Directs building the large size first and simplifying down for smaller sizes — never designing the small size first
results.evidence: Start by designing your icons at 32px or even 40px ... Never design the small size first and enlarge it

results.expectation: Requires all strokes in a set to share one weight and warns against mixing filled and stroked icons side by side without intention
results.evidence: All strokes in your icon set must share the same weight ... Don't mix filled and stroked icons side by side without a clear structural reason

results.expectation: States the gap between strokes must be at least the stroke weight, or that edge padding equal to the stroke weight balances visual weight (or aligning straight lines to the pixel grid with an optical grid for perceptual center)
results.evidence: The gap between strokes must be at least equal to the stroke weight itself
